wiki_catalogs.name: Capability Inventory: What Is Already Built
wiki_catalogs.description: Capability Inventory: What Is Already Built
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Headline index of the shipped surface: one glanceable matrix of every capability area below with its implementing package path, its evidence (source + test + example route), and its remaining gate. Frame it as 'implemented in code, pending owner evaluation'.

wiki_catalogs.name: Compilation Pipeline — Implemented
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Inventory the mdsvex compile layer as shipped: GFM, frontmatter handling, heading slugs/anchors, semantic table wrapping, Shiki dual-theme code frames, fence metadata, mermaid guard, HTML rendering parity for Studio/validate, and source-safety diagnostics — each with its file in packages/mdsvex/src.

wiki_catalogs.name: Positioning & Operating Model
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Compare operating models: Blume as a zero-config CLI-driven Astro site the tool owns (with eject), Scribe as a compile-time publishing layer for a Next.js/Vite site you own, Acrolls as a SvelteKit-native publishing SDK where the host keeps routing and the framework owns article and docs-shell rendering.

wiki_catalogs.name: P0 Blockers & Repair Sequence
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Turn the currently open, evidence-less items into an ordered, gated sequence: packed CLI and public-package verification, reconciliation of stale task/checklist/onboarding guidance with the implemented content API, source-level styling-rule audit, and full browser acceptance of nav, TOC, pager, persistence, accessibility, and console errors.

wiki_catalogs.name: Article Components & Styling System — Implemented
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Inventory the reader-facing component surface (Publication, PublicationLayout, Banner, Callout, Figure, Video, ZoomableImage, code-frame and mermaid client enhancers) and the styling layers (foundation/default/colors/theme/docs/tokens SASS + CSS entrypoints, fractalthemer theming kit, CUBE CSS discipline).

wiki_catalogs.name: Feature Comparison: Acrolls vs. Blume vs. Scribe
wiki_catalogs.description: Feature Comparison: Acrolls vs. Blume vs. Scribe
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Headline page for the comparative axis: what each product is for, who owns the site, and where the three overlap or diverge. Establish the comparison method (repo evidence vs. dated external claims) before any matrix.

wiki_catalogs.name: Authoring & Rendering Features
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Compare the authoring experience feature by feature: content format (MDX vs Markdown/mdsvex/.svx), component availability inside content, islands/auto-hydration, includes, math, callout/syntax breadth, code-block capabilities (highlighting, filename, line actions, copy/wrap), tables, and images/video.

wiki_catalogs.name: Release Engineering & Distribution
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Specify the engineering work required to ship credibly at scale: versioning and changelog policy, CI matrix (OS + package manager + packed-consumer install/build), release automation, tarball contents audit, deprecation policy for the legacy generated-source helper, and support infrastructure (issues, discussions, CONTRIBUTING, security posture).

wiki_catalogs.name: Docs Shell & Navigation — Implemented
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Inventory the docs chrome that exists: DocsShell and the sidebar-only composition, accordion nav tree, breadcrumbs, pager, TOC, page header, mobile drawer, localStorage open-state persistence, and the pure nav helpers with deterministic node identity.

wiki_catalogs.name: Site Structure: Navigation, Versioning, i18n, Sources
wiki_catalogs.description: Site Structure: Navigation, Versioning, i18n, Sources
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Compare information-architecture features: file-convention nav vs Acrolls' explicit host-defined page tree, folder meta overrides, breadcrumbs/pager/TOC, multi-source content (local/remote/backend), docs versioning and locale routing, and where Acrolls is ahead or simply absent.

wiki_catalogs.name: Launch Readiness: Path to an Industry-Class Docs Framework
wiki_catalogs.description: Launch Readiness: Path to an Industry-Class Docs Framework
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Headline page for the launch axis: define what 'industry-class' means as measurable gates, summarize the P0 blocker set, and give the ordered path through the child workstreams with dependencies between them.

wiki_catalogs.name: Feature Parity Workplan
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Lay out the feature work needed to compete with the compared products, each item sized and ordered with its entry point in the existing code: search packaging beyond raw Pagefind, RSS feeds, blog/changelog index pages, doc versioning, i18n, a content-component set (tabs, steps, cards, code groups), API-reference generation, MCP/agent surface beyond the static tier, and a `create acrolls` scaffold plus a docs/marketing site.

wiki_catalogs.name: Content Source & Collection API — Implemented
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Inventory how a host declares its corpus today: the collection API with optional Standard Schema validation, blessed page/post/changelog field schemas, loader merging, naming conventions, hidden-vs-filter semantics, the pluggable loader seam, and the deprecated generated-source helper still in support.

wiki_catalogs.name: Discoverability, SEO & AI-Agent Surfaces
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Compare the machine-readability and growth layer: SEO metadata, sitemap/robots, OG images, RSS, JSON-LD, analytics, search (client vs hosted vs semantic), llms.txt and Markdown mirrors, MCP servers, in-page Ask AI, doc evals, translation automation, and PDF/EPUB export — crediting what Acrolls already ships and naming what it does not.

wiki_catalogs.name: Quality Bar: Accessibility, Performance, Types & DX
wiki_catalogs.description: Quality Bar: Accessibility, Performance, Types & DX
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Define the non-functional bar an industry-class framework is judged on and the current gap: keyboard/screen-reader coverage for generated nav, reduced-motion and print behavior, JS payload and lazy-loading budgets, SSR/prerender correctness, type surface quality for hosts, and documentation/DX polish (handbook, snippets, examples, llms.txt freshness).

wiki_catalogs.name: SEO, Search, OG & Agent Surface — Implemented
wiki_catalogs.description: SEO, Search, OG & Agent Surface — Implemented
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Inventory the discoverability layer that ships: SEO builder plus sitemap/robots, the DocsSeo component, OG card generation, Pagefind-integrated search with the body/ignore markers, copy-page-markdown, and the llms.txt / llms-full.txt / per-page Markdown agent surface — including how examples/kit-consumer wires each as a route.

wiki_catalogs.name: CLI, Configuration & Extensibility
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Compare the operator experience: single-command onboarding (blume init, scribe integrate, acrolls onboard/integrate), config surface (blume.config.ts vs code + entrypoints), customization depth (component overrides, registry, custom pages, eject vs host-owned components), theming story, and agent-readiness of each CLI.

wiki_catalogs.name: Launch Checklist & Go/No-Go Criteria
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Close the wiki with a single executable launch checklist: prerequisite gates from the blocker workstream, the docs/marketing site, first-host case studies, announcement assets, and explicit no-go conditions — written so a third party can run it without inference.

wiki_catalogs.name: CLI, Studio & Corpus Preflight — Implemented
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Inventory the author/tooling surface that ships: onboard checkpoints and modes, integrate as the single reviewed mutation path, init and docs init, validate with authored/migration modes and error-page policy, and the localhost Studio preview — with the stable exit-code and JSON contracts.

wiki_catalogs.name: Gap Analysis Matrix & Differentiators
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Consolidate every child comparison into one matrix (shipped / partial / absent per product) and then argue the differentiators Acrolls can actually defend: Svelte-native rendering with no runtime lock-in, article typography and accessibility depth, compile-time Shiki, corpus preflight with migration policy, CUBE-aligned SASS theming, and deterministic host-owned page trees.

wiki_catalogs.name: Package Surface, Release & Evidence Harness
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Inventory the distribution and proof machinery: the public entrypoint list, bundledDependencies layout, published version on npm, the documented release sequence, the packed-consumer verification script, the example host with its /acceptance smoke route, and the per-package test files that exist.
